newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev eases to 1,000 vs mark, falls on dlr.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev eases to 1,000 vs mark, falls on dlr.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev opened at 999-1000 per mark on Wednesday, down from 998-999 at Tuesday's close as banks were bidding for marks to profit on higher foreign currency interbank deposit rates.
* Banks were buying marks near the central bank currency board ask price of 1,000 levs.
* Interbank overnight lev depo rates now stand at 1.50-1.75 percent annually against 3.0 percent on overnight mark deposits and around five percent on dollar deposits.
* The lev opened at 1,837-1,839 to the dollar, softer from 1,825-1,829 at Tuesday's close, tracking the dollar/mark cross on global markets.
* Local traders adjust the lev/dollar to the lev/mark and the international mark/dollar crosses.
* The lev has been pegged at 1,000 to the mark as an anchor in an IMF-prescribed currency board system, a fixed exchange rate mechanism introduced on July 1 to restore confidence in the lev.
* Under the system Bulgaria's central bank pledged to buy and sell unlimited volumes of the anchor currency at a fixed bid of 995 levs and ask of 1,000.
